row.scim_plan: Starter (all plans; Bring Your Own Identity Provider entitlement)
row.evidence: Qlik Help says Qlik Cloud is compatible with SCIM 2.0 and that the only supported SCIM connector is Microsoft Entra ID; SCIM needs the Bring Your Own Identity Provider entitlement, which the pricing comparison ticks on every plan from Starter up.
row.notes: New row. Partial because SCIM works with exactly one IdP: Qlik Help lists Microsoft Entra ID as the only SCIM connector, configured as a non-gallery Entra enterprise app with the tenant URL and token from Administration > Identity provider > Manage auto provisioning, and an active Entra interactive IdP is required first. Price-wise SCIM is not gated: the pricing comparison ticks Bring Your Own Identity Provider and Enterprise single sign-on on Starter, Standard, Premium and Enterprise. Pricing is capacity-based, not per user: Starter $300/mo includes 10 users, Standard $825/mo (25 GB, no cost for additional users), Premium $2,750/mo (50 GB), Enterprise quote; all billed annually, so per-user fields are null. SCIM deprovisioning marks users Disabled (cannot log in); admins can then delete them. Okta, Auth0 and other OIDC/SAML IdPs are supported for sign-in only; Okta's OIN 'Qlik' app is SWA only. Qlik Talend Cloud (the data-integration product) has its own separate SCIM API with Okta and Azure AD guides; this row covers Qlik Cloud Analytics. A full REST user API (users, groups, roles, licence assignments, audits, webhooks) is documented on qlik.dev; the pricing page lists APIs on every plan.

scim.plan: Starter (all plans; Bring Your Own Identity Provider entitlement)

auth.token_source: Administration activity center > Identity provider > (Entra ID configuration) > Manage auto provisioning > Enable
auth.notes: The token expires and must be renewed manually in Qlik Cloud, but the lifetime is not stated. The token is stored as an API key of subType externalClient.

operations.notes: Create, update and remove are described from Entra's side; PUT vs PATCH is not stated. SCIM group endpoints cover list, get, delete and patch of IdP-managed groups.

deprovision.data_retained: User is marked Disabled and cannot log in; admins can delete the user afterwards and are encouraged to reassign ownership of apps, data connections and data files.

custom.how: Entra mappings must be cut down to the five required attributes or provisioning fails.

attributes.notes: The help page lists the Entra source expressions to keep; the SCIM target names are only shown in screenshots, so the target names here are inferred from Entra's default mapping and should be checked.

roles.how: Roles are not set over SCIM; after provisioning an admin assigns security roles to the provisioned groups in Administration > Manage users > Permissions.

limitations.text: Only Microsoft Entra ID is a supported SCIM connector, and it needs Entra ID P1 or higher.
Users in nested groups are not provisioned.
Custom groups created in Qlik Cloud are not visible to or changed by SCIM.
The SCIM token expires and must be renewed manually in Qlik Cloud and pasted into Entra.
Each tenant can have only one active interactive IdP at a time.

auth.notes: API keys carry the creating user's permissions and cannot be scoped; OAuth2 clients (including machine-to-machine) support scopes.

capabilities.notes: POST /api/v1/users creates an invited user. Deactivate and reactivate are a JSON Patch on /status (statuses active, invited, disabled, deleted, provisioned).

endpoints.purpose: Update user (name, assignedRoles, assignedGroups, status, locale)

rate_limits.text: Per-endpoint tiers, e.g. List users Tier 1 (1000 requests per minute); create/update/delete user Tier 2 (100 requests per minute).

limitations.text: API keys cannot be scoped and carry the full permissions of the user who created them.
Legacy com.qlik.v1.user.* events are deprecated and removed on or after November 30, 2026.

okta.notes: OIN 'Qlik' app (last updated Jun. 21 2018) has only SWA ticked among its functionality filters. Qlik Help documents Okta as a SAML/OIDC IdP for sign-in (custom app), not for SCIM.

entra.notes: Qlik Cloud SCIM uses a non-gallery Entra enterprise app ('Create your own application'). The Entra gallery tutorial found covers Qlik Sense Enterprise Client-Managed (on-premises, SAML with JIT), not Qlik Cloud.

open_questions: SCIM token lifetime is not stated (docs only say it expires and must be renewed manually).
Whether a SCIM DELETE removes the user or only disables it, and whether disabling frees the user licence, is not documented.
The SCIM base URL pattern and supported filters, pagination and PUT vs PATCH are not published; the tenant URL is shown in the admin console.
Exact SCIM target attribute names are only shown in screenshots on the Entra setup page.
Whether Qlik Cloud creates users just-in-time on first SSO sign-in is not stated on the pages read.
No Qlik Cloud app found in the Entra gallery, Google, OneLogin or JumpCloud catalogues.
